A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SUPERDIFF research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original CIFAR-10, Stable Diffusion composition, and protein-generation experiments, with quantitative tables and generated examples.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds multi-property small-molecule generation results in Section 4.4, Table 4, and Appendix I.

M1.justification: The documented AND weight computation changes: v1 solves Aκ+b=1 and then normalizes κ; v2 jointly solves for normalized weights and a shared density increment using an augmented system (Proposition 6, Appendix C.1). The OR procedure and density-estimation formulas remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds a distinct application domain: text-conditioned small-molecule generation using LDMol, targeting GSK3β inhibition jointly with either drug-likeness (QED) or JNK3 inhibition. Existing image and protein tasks remain, including the relocated Stable Diffusion OR experiments.

E2.justification: The new molecule comparison includes separately evaluated single-property LDMol controls, P1 only and P2 only, alongside reused joint-prompting and score-averaging strategies (Table 4). Comparator membership in the retained image and protein experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 introduces a substantial molecular evaluation protocol: batches of 512, top-10/top-1 selection, property products and minima, oracle scoring, fingerprint diversity, validity/uniqueness, and quality thresholds. Joint prompting balances both property orderings equally. These are new evaluation settings; retained experiments show no substantive protocol revision.

E4.justification: Appendix I adds qualitative case studies comparing top SUPERDIFF and score-averaged molecules, displaying structures and both target-property scores (Figures A3–A4). The OR image case study also replaces several random-prompt baseline examples. Existing protein analyses remain; no substantial new ablation or robustness program appears.

E5.justification: Table 4 explicitly reports five runs for the new molecule experiments and provides ± uncertainty for property scores. Existing FLD/protein uncertainty reporting and image-seed information remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish increased repetition of retained experiments.

E6.justification: V2 adds molecular results: Table 4 reports SUPERDIFF top-10 property products of 0.177 versus 0.154 for averaging on GSK3β/QED, and 0.080 versus 0.073 on GSK3β/JNK3. These are new comparisons, not improvements over v1 under matched conditions. Existing numerical tables retain their values; several OR baseline example images change.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 replaces the solve-then-normalize argument with an augmented system enforcing equal density changes and weight normalization simultaneously. Appendix D adds explicit Hutchinson variance calculations and distinguishes its randomness from generation noise. The principal superposition and Itô-density results are retained, with localized proof corrections.

C1.justification: The abstract adds improved conditional molecule generation to the application claims. The introduction qualifies the estimator's exactness by requiring ground-truth marginal scores. The central claims about inference-time superposition, OR/AND composition, and efficient density estimation remain.

C2.justification: V2 drops v1's categorical assertion that averaging cannot improve over either constituent protein model. Appendix D clarifies the different randomness underlying the estimator-variance comparison, and Section 4.4 interprets molecular results as simultaneous property control. The stated computational limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds implementation access links for SUPERDIFF with Stable Diffusion v1-4 and SDXL. It also documents molecular prompt templates, the LDMol base model, scoring oracles, fingerprints, and quality thresholds. Existing image and protein implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 acknowledges independently related density estimators from Karczewski et al., credits Peluchetti for continuous-mixture extensions, and adds molecular-generation and evaluation references. The existing protein-related-work discussion moves to Appendix E rather than being removed.

P1.justification: V2 locally condenses and rewrites the image/protein discussion, moves Stable Diffusion OR material to Appendix J.1 and protein related work to Appendix E, and updates publication headers and acknowledgments. Most exposition and the overall theoretical organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 separates the OR portion of Table 2 into Appendix Table A2, adds molecular Table 4 and Figures A3–A4, reformats protein UMAP panels, and replaces OR baseline thumbnails. The 20 AND image-comparison grids are retained with renumbering; the overall visual design remains similar.

improvement.justification: Replacing v1's solve-then-normalize step with joint constraints improves the documented AND procedure, while the exactness and variance clarifications improve technical precision. New molecule experiments add useful evidence of broader applicability with five-run reporting. Their advantages are modest and mixed across metrics, supporting a limited overall quality improvement.
